shininho.title: Shininho
pipeline: OptiTrack / Motive body + separate iPhone face
decisions: Prototype lost likeness
Rebuild from the high-resolution source instead of accepting a functional but less recognizable character.
Source / prototype / MetaHuman comparison.
chapter-01
Low-floor capture broke down
Retake visible failures; reconstruct residual damaged ranges with valid neighboring poses.
Capture-stage documentation and the documented repair method.
chapter-04
Body and face were recorded separately
Keep independent take selection, then align the chosen performances.
Facial-capture footage and final Unreal performance.
chapter-03
shininho.handoff: A MetaHuman-compatible character, cleaned and retargeted body animation, independently selected facial animation, and assembled Unreal performance. The later VR scene adds immersive staging and hand-driven effects.
shininho.review: Review source-to-final likeness, eyes in motion, continuity through reconstructed ranges, body / face timing, and the complete scene presentation.

slots.name: One take, four views
slots.record: Use the same source take and time range. Add a shared frame counter and annotate one tracking-loss range, the correction, and the final body contact. Keep a raw / corrected curve inset for the edited joint.
slots.pass: All four views identify the same take and frame range; correction ranges are marked; the result can be inspected at normal speed and frame by frame.
slots.copy: I reconstructed the marked tracking-loss segment using valid neighboring poses, then reviewed the corrected body performance against reference before combining the independently selected facial take in Unreal.

slots.name: Capture decision on stage
slots.record: Show the actual operator, equipment, calibration record if retained, take direction, one visible source failure, and the resulting retake. State when archival footage does not cover a step.
slots.pass: Direct capture operation and downstream preparation are attributable; no external volumetric-studio work is presented as my acquisition.
slots.copy: The stage review connected performer direction to data usability: I checked the problematic movement, directed a retake, and preserved the selected take for downstream cleanup.

row.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
pipeline: Look development + canon + head / body alignment
decisions: Some identity input was unusable
Recover with supplemental Polycam source, then review each person individually.
Identity-pipeline images and ten-face grid.
chapter-01
Five overlapping close-up faces
Retain LOD 0; adjust groom response and disable unnecessary groom simulation.
Skin / groom comparisons and overlap evidence.
chapter-02
Singing sources lacked editorial coverage
Rebuild silent beats while retaining useful blinking and subtle head motion.
Sequencer, reconstruction, and final ensemble views.
chapter-03
row.handoff: Ten individualized characters organized into two five-character ensembles, canon-timed facial performances, morning / sunset / night lighting variants, and a looping two-channel presentation for square panels.
row.review: Review each identity against its reference, ensemble skin / groom readability, silent-to-singing continuity, stable head motion, and the intended front / side installation framing.

slots.name: One editorial beat, source to ensemble
slots.record: Show one participant through an entrance or pause. Identify removed mouth keys, retained blinks, the head-motion representation, and the same moment in the ensemble.
slots.pass: The comparison uses a matching time window and clearly separates artist-recorded input from my identity, editorial, and integration work.
slots.copy: I rebuilt the missing editorial beat from the singing source, retained useful blinking and head movement, and aligned the body-side head motion before reviewing the character in the canon ensemble.

slots.name: Ensemble delivery record
slots.record: Record actual engine version, hardware, character / groom settings, output resolution, delivery frame rate, and render time. Define the baseline before making a cost comparison.
slots.pass: Every number comes from the actual scene or delivery; appearance and cost are reported separately; front / side and channel framing are visible.
slots.copy: I reviewed the five-character overlap in the final framing, then recorded the scene settings and delivered the two-channel loop using the documented output configuration.

gang-se-hwang.title: Gang Se-hwang
pipeline: Unity HDRP character + C# museum interaction
decisions: Only painted likeness was available
Anchor the visible likeness to the portrait; interpret unseen anatomy as production geometry.
Portrait reconstruction and wireframe / UV evidence.
chapter-01
Capture coefficients did not map
Normalize channel-name case in an existing import workflow.
Custom rig evidence and facial-performance comparison.
chapter-02
Different assets needed different playback behavior
Use card hair for the real-time character and garment caches synchronized in Timeline.
Hair-card, Hanbok, Unity, and public-kiosk evidence.
chapter-03
gang-se-hwang.handoff: A custom historical character, capture-driven facial targets, card hair, synchronized Hanbok caches, HDRP look development, and a visitor-facing Unity / C# application.
gang-se-hwang.review: Review likeness from the portrait view, expression correspondence, eye / mouth deformation, garment timing, character appearance at kiosk scale, and visitor interaction.

slots.name: Trace a coefficient into the custom face
slots.record: Select a real recorded channel and expression. Show the import mismatch and fix, relevant target weights, and the same expression on the finished face. Identify inherited and authored components.
slots.pass: The captured signal reaches the correct channel; the expression is inspectable in motion; expanded targets are not described as 256 independent ARKit channels.
slots.copy: I traced the recorded coefficient through the imported workflow, corrected the channel-name mismatch, and reviewed the relevant base and corrective shapes on the custom character.

slots.name: One interaction from input to display
slots.record: Record the actual touch or trigger, the Unity event / state, character timing, camera composite, and deployed screen. Avoid invented uptime or reliability statistics.
slots.pass: The complete interaction is visible and its scope is attributable; garment / animation timing and the live camera feed can be reviewed together.
slots.copy: The visitor input triggers the character presentation while the live camera feed and UI remain coordinated in the public Unity application.

when-it-seen.title: When It Seen
pipeline: Independent timing alignment for three dancers
Full body + face Alembic; no clothing
decisions: Sources came from independent streams
Align each dancer before baking the combined performance.
Capture and integrated-performance videos.
chapter-02
The receiving department needed a moving surface
Deliver body and facial deformation as full-character Alembic.
Integrated character and credited downstream cloth-contact footage.
chapter-03
when-it-seen.handoff: Per-performer, synchronized full-character Alembic geometry carrying both body and facial deformation for the collaborating Houdini department. Clothing simulation belongs to that downstream team.
when-it-seen.review: Review the selected timing for each dancer, facial inclusion, geometry continuity, source / export range agreement, and the receiving department’s interpretation of the cache.

slots.name: Round-trip the receiving surface
slots.record: Use one dancer and matched frames. Record actual range, rate, units, up axis, included meshes, format, and receiving application. Ask the receiving team to identify its import and simulation contribution.
slots.pass: Body and face are present at matching frames, timing / scale are documented, and downstream simulation is credited separately.
slots.copy: I compared the synchronized character in Unreal with the imported body-and-face cache at matched frames before the receiving team used the surface for cloth-contact simulation.

graphics-rd.title: Erick Oh collaboration
decisions: Interactive droplets needed a coherent liquid appearance
Separate C# object behavior from the raymarched HLSL field.
Runtime / Unity footage and the documented division of responsibilities.
chapter-02
Growth needed repeatable art direction
Preserve vertex count and ordering across exactly four Maya targets.
Four growth states and multi-view wireframes.
chapter-03
graphics-rd.handoff: Controllable Unity URP visual systems, C# behavior / material controls, and four corresponding Maya-authored deformation states driven through Timeline / Animation.
graphics-rd.review: Review input-to-visual response, grouping behavior versus appearance, target correspondence, and artist control of repeatable growth.

slots.name: Expose the behavior and rendering contract
slots.record: Record one shareable input / parameter change and its corresponding code / material control and output. Use only cleared source; a newly authored reference implementation must be labeled as such.
slots.pass: The relationship between input and visual behavior is inspectable; existing project code and new reference code are clearly distinguished.
slots.copy: C# maps the runtime control to the material parameters, while HLSL determines the visible cloud or liquid response. The breakdown shows the same change at each layer.

age-variation.title: Age-variant digital human
decisions: Age changes affected different representations
Use a separate body adaptation for the child and surface changes on the shared adult geometry.
Identity-development images and age-state comparison.
chapter-02
age-variation.handoff: A shared facial reference across a child-body adaptation and adult age treatments. Adult transitions are material / texture changes, with the child body handled as a separate structural adaptation.
age-variation.review: Review facial recognition across the states, the child head / body junction, adult-geometry consistency, and the transition under a fixed camera and light.

slots.name: Separate structure from surface
slots.record: Keep camera and lighting fixed for adult surface transitions. Include a wireframe view and identify the separate child-body branch without implying a single mesh morphs through every age.
slots.pass: Shared adult geometry and the separate child-body adaptation are explicit; changes can be inspected without camera or lighting confounds.
slots.copy: The adult treatments preserve the same geometry while surface parameters change. The child variant uses a separate body adaptation to address the younger silhouette.
